transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-05-12 11:00 AM PT
Duration: 40 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Alex Rivera (ClarityHealth - Head of ML), Priya Singh (CTO), Jordan Kim (Eng Manager)

[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, I'm on the account team here at Redwood. With me is Liam Chen, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:22] Alex Rivera: Doing well, thanks. Excited to see the model catalog walk-through. We've been looking at open models and trying to figure out which ones make sense for our clinical summarization workloads.
[00:45] Priya Singh: Hi, thanks for setting this up. A quick note: security is a big factor for us — SOC 2, KMS, and VPC options are must-haves.
[01:10] Maya Patel: Totally understood, we'll touch on deployment modes and security. Liam, do you want to start on the catalog?
[01:20] Liam Chen: Yup. So, the model catalog is our curated list of open models plus Redwood-verified performance profiles. On the left you see model metadata — architecture, typical latencies, token cost, and whether we support quantization profiles. We also publish benchmark telemetry like p50/p95 latency at different sequence lengths and hardware profiles.
[01:45] Jordan Kim: Are those benchmarks run on hosted infra or our dedicated env?
[01:55] Liam Chen: Good question. The catalog shows both hosted numbers (our public fleet) and numbers we've seen on Dedicated with similar GPU configs — we annotate which numbers are from which environment. For Private deployments we provide a compatibility matrix showing expected perf by GPU type and quantization.
[02:25] Alex Rivera: When you say 'compatibility matrix,' can you show an example? We need to know if a 4-bit quantized model will run on our A100s or the customer's upcoming H100s.
[02:40] Liam Chen: Yeah — here's the matrix. For each model variant (fp16, int8, 4-bit q4, etc) we list supported hardware and any kernel caveats. For example some 4-bit paths are optimized for Ampere vs Hopper and may need different kernel selection. Note: sometimes the transcription might show 'K-V cash' — we mean KV cache.
[03:05] Priya Singh: That's helpful. We have strict latency SLOs for the summarization pipeline — p95 under 1.2s for 512 tokens is our target. Can you point to models that hit that with reasonable cost?
[03:25] Liam Chen: On hosted we see models A, B, and C hitting p95 ~0.9–1.1s at 512 tokens on our 8xA10 profile with batching disabled. Model B is a strong cost/latency sweet spot; Model A is slightly higher quality but more expensive. We can run an apples-to-apples benchmark with your sample prompts to validate.
[03:55] Alex Rivera: What's the trade when we move to Dedicated or Private? We want predictable latency and data isolation.
[04:10] Maya Patel: Dedicated gives you reserved capacity — predictable throughput and isolation — and you can pin model versions. Private (VPC/on-prem) gives you full network isolation and control of KMS/HSM for keys. In Private deployments we can still provide the same runtime but you manage the infra.
[04:35] Jordan Kim: Any differences in model performance between Hosted and Dedicated?
[04:45] Liam Chen: Performance is similar if you pick comparable GPU shapes and kernel stacks. Differences usually come from packing/utilization and whether our autoscaler is sharing nodes. With Dedicated, you're guaranteed the pool and can tune things like prewarmed kernels, batching policies, and cache residency.
[05:10] Priya Singh: About quantization — we've seen quality regressions in some earlier evals. How does Redwood handle quantization recommendations?
[05:25] Liam Chen: We run quantization profiles per model with evaluation prompts and report a quality delta vs fp16. In the catalog we show recommended quantization levels by workload type — e.g., classification vs summarization. For summarization we often recommend int8 or q4_0 for latency-sensitive setups but we surface a quality delta and an eval harness.
[05:50] Alex Rivera: Can you point to the eval harness? Is it something we can run?
[05:58] Liam Chen: Yes, we can provide the eval scripts and the benchmark spreadsheet. We'll share the doc after the call. It includes per-prompt metrics, ROUGE/BLEU-ish analogs we use, and cost-per-1k tokens calculations.
[06:20] Maya Patel: We'll also include an example compatibility matrix — it's a CSV tied to the catalog.
[06:30] Priya Singh: Security again — for Private we need KMS + HSM details and audit logs; do you support customer-managed keys?
[06:40] Liam Chen: Yes, for Private we integrate with customer KMS (we've done AWS KMS and HashiCorp Vault integrations). For Hosted we support customer-managed keys in some enterprise engagements; for Dedicated we can set up a KMS bridge. We'll attach the security docs.
[07:05] Jordan Kim: Latency vs cost: can you show how Optimize recommendations change unit economics?
[07:15] Liam Chen: Sure. Optimize is our toolkit that looks at batching, automatic KV prefix caching, and model selection. For example, enabling prefix caching on repeated clinical templates can reduce token cost by 20–50% and also cut effective latency for subsequent messages. We have a small interactive chart in the Console showing throughput vs per-token cost per model.
[07:45] Alex Rivera: Does caching introduce correctness concerns for our use case? We generate summaries for PHI content, so we need to ensure we don't leak across tenants or persist data incorrectly.
[07:58] Liam Chen: Caching respects tenant isolation — per-tenant caches. For Private deployments, you control cache eviction and retention policies. We'll add a note in the security doc about cache controls.
[08:20] Maya Patel: Time for a quick demo — Liam, can you share screen and walk the model catalog UI?
[08:30] Liam Chen: (screen share) On the top is the search bar: you can filter by task (summarization), architecture, quantization support, and latency profile. Clicking into a model shows verified benchmarks, a link to the eval harness, and the compatibility matrix. Here's Model B's page — quality metrics, p50/p95 at seq lengths 128/512/1024, and an expected cost per 1k tokens.
[09:05] Priya Singh: Are those numbers synthetic or derived from customer workloads?
[09:12] Liam Chen: A mix. We run a synthetic benchmark across representative prompts and also anonymized telemetry from consenting customers. When customers run pilots, we append their numbers to a private workspace so you can compare.
[09:30] Alex Rivera: We'd like the pilot numbers to be kept private.
[09:34] Maya Patel: Absolutely — pilot telemetry is only visible to your team and Redwood's SEs on the deal.
[09:45] Jordan Kim: What about model rollouts and version pinning? We can't have silent quality regressions.
[09:55] Liam Chen: You can pin a model version at route-level. We also support canary rollouts and automatic regression alerts tied to prompt sets. If a new model deviates beyond thresholds we can auto-fallback to a pinned variant.
[10:15] Alex Rivera: Nice. How does function/tool calling or structured output fit into the catalog? We have a structured extraction step downstream.
[10:26] Liam Chen: We annotate model capabilities — some models are better at structured output. In the catalog we tag models that have been validated on structured extraction tasks. You can also run constrained decoding profiles via the runtime.
[10:40] Priya Singh: For Dedicated, how do pricing tiers work? We have predictable budget constraints.
[10:48] Maya Patel: Dedicated is committed capacity — monthly or annual. We'll send a pricing sheet with example configurations (small/medium/large pools) and an estimated pilot cost. Hosted remains pay-as-you-go. We'll include cost modeling in the spreadsheet.
[11:10] Alex Rivera: For the pilot, we'd like a 2-week run with 50k requests total, a mixed distribution of short and long prompts. We'll provide the prompt set. Can you estimate the infra we'd need?
[11:25] Liam Chen: We'll run a sizing exercise — if you share the QPS distribution and prompt lengths we can map to GPU shape and required concurrency. We'll also propose a Dedicated pool or Hosted burst plan depending on the desired isolation.
[11:40] Jordan Kim: Any gotchas with quantization on Hopper vs Ampere? We have some H100 infra coming.
[11:48] Liam Chen: Yes, certain 4-bit kernels are Hopper-optimized; some q4 flavors run better on H100 with the latest kernel set. We'll flag that in the compatibility matrix. Also, some vendor toolchains produce different perf numbers — we'll include notes.
[12:05] Alex Rivera: Are you able to run a benchmark on our H100s if we give you access, or do you prefer we run it and share results?
[12:14] Maya Patel: We can support both models; typically we provide an automated benchmark script you can run and also offer to run it for you if you prefer. For Private/on-prem we usually hand over scripts.
[12:28] Priya Singh: What's the SLA on Dedicated?
[12:33] Maya Patel: We offer SLA-backed uptime and latency targets for Dedicated enterprise tiers. We'll include specific SLAs in the enterprise packet.
[12:42] Alex Rivera: Quick question on observability — can we get token-level cost breakdowns and per-route dashboards?
[12:50] Liam Chen: Yes, Console has per-route metrics, token-level cost breakdowns, traces, and error analysis. You can hook custom tracing IDs too.
[13:05] Jordan Kim: Any mention of competitors — we've looked at Bedrock and Anthropic; how does Redwood differ?
[13:15] Maya Patel: We focus on production inference tooling for open models — unified runtime + routing + Optimize recommendations and transparent benchmarks. Bedrock is a broad managed service; Anthropic/OpenAI are model providers. We differentiate on observability, cost controls, and deployment flexibility.
[13:40] Alex Rivera: Sounds good. Next steps?
[13:45] Maya Patel: We'll do the following: Liam will export the model catalog benchmark spreadsheet and the compatibility matrix; I'll send security docs and pricing tiers; Alex, you'll share sample prompts and QPS profile. Then we'll kick off a 2-week pilot starting next week if timelines align.
[14:05] Priya Singh: One last thing — audit logs retention and SSO. We use Okta.
[14:13] Liam Chen: SSO via SAML/Okta is supported. Audit logs and retention windows are configurable in Dedicated and Private.
[14:25] Alex Rivera: Great. Thanks everyone.
[14:30] Maya Patel: Thanks — we'll follow up with the docs.
[14:35] (some participants leave)
[16:00] End of recording
